pull: Clue: America's top ace flew one
body:
Can you name this aircraft?

On Thanksgiving Day, 25 November 1943, American fighters of this type flew from China with B-25 bombers in the Fourteenth Air Force's first attack on Formosa, now Taiwan. They struck the Japanese airfield at Shinchiku, and the Americans claimed more than 30 Japanese planes destroyed in the air and on the ground.

The clue is on the card. Drop your guess below.
photoNote: Fifteenth Air Force P-38 Lightnings of a fighter group in Italy flying in formation, 1944 (print received by the Army Air Forces in November 1944). Not the Shinchiku raid and not the Fourteenth Air Force; the same type, a year later. U.S. Air Force photo 55553AC, NARA 342-FH-3A22848 (NAID 204907489). Tier: green, U.S. government work, public domain. Cropped to the photo inside the print border; tail serials and squadron numbers visible but nothing names the type.
photoCredit: P-38 Lightnings of the Fifteenth Air Force in formation over Italy, 1944. U.S. Air Force 55553AC, National Archives, public domain.
